Touchpoints
Too little room to review candidates.

Touchpoints

Two tabs, because docs/touchpoints.md says each subject has one pane and separate subjects get separate panes. The class tab opens on a saved result from March, which is the behaviour the document is most emphatic about: Wikipedia results have no automatic expiry and a valid saved entry is reused regardless of its age. The individual tab has no saved entry, so it shows what an unsearched pane looks like.

Things worth doing in it

Press Refresh on the class tabThe first attempt is throttled. The saved rows stay on screen, the error says how long the wait is and that a repeat doubles it, and nothing is retried automatically. Press it again and it succeeds, the fetch date becomes now, and one candidate appears that the saved copy did not have.
Select a rowIts relationship and target controls appear inside the row, and the statement it will write is printed underneath. A title, alias or redirect match starts at skos:exactMatch; everything else starts at skos:closeMatch.
Switch a relationship to rdfs:seeAlsoThe target changes to Wikipedia, because that is the documented default for that predicate. Wikidata is only offered when Wikipedia reported an item ID.
Select Scholarly communication and applyIt has no DBpedia resource. The whole batch is rejected and the row is named, because validation rejects the batch if any selected statement is unavailable or invalid. Change its target to Wikipedia and the batch applies.
Use the menu to change the ontology, then applyApply refuses and asks you to search again, which is the documented rule for a store that moved under a result.
Turn the local model off in the menuThe ranking column disappears and the order reverts to Wikipedia's. With MPNet present the rows are reordered using the label, parents and description. Neither path calls Claude or Codex.
Try the disambiguation rowIt cannot be selected, and the row says so rather than failing at apply time.

Why nothing withdraws when the pane gets shallow

Every other view in this set drops a region on height. This one must not. Its policy row reads "Header, query and footer remain around results", and the acceptance line is blunter: "With Touchpoints ready, Search and Refresh remain visible without scrolling. Selected candidates have a reachable Apply action." So the results scroller absorbs the whole loss and the three bands stay. On width, the target IRI withdraws below 600 and the relationship control narrows, which is the published narrow behaviour.

One published number this does not follow

The document says Touchpoints, Inspector and Individuals "register recovery below 240 pixels wide or 120 pixels tall", while the shared ladder in the same document gives recovery "below 240 wide, 210 high when narrow, 180 otherwise". Those two sentences disagree about height. This file uses the shared ladder, 240 and 180, because the whole point of the set is one measurement model; the pane also keeps the subject and the query visible in recovery, which is what the Touchpoints clause was protecting. If you want the 120 instead, it is one number in one container query.

What is simulated rather than live

No request leaves this file. The candidate lists, their descriptions, item IDs, redirect flags and existing links are seeded, the first Refresh is a scripted 429, and the search has a short artificial delay so the in flight state is visible. The cache path, the User-Agent policy and the fifteen second timeout are quoted in the footer and the menu rather than performed.
